                                      PROJECT NO. 59142

    REVIEW OF ERCOT’S                            §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES                    §
    FOR LARGE LOADS
                                                 §                   OF TEXAS

                            JOINT COMMENTS OF
                STREAM DATA CENTERS, L.P. AND PROVIDENT CORP.
                        REGARDING ERCOT’S PGRR 145

        Stream Data Centers, L.P. (Stream) and Provident Corp. (Provident) (collectively Joint

Commenters) appreciate the opportunity to provide these comments regarding ERCOT’s Planning

Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145. In its April 4, 2026, comments on PGRR 145, ERCOT

expressed its expectation that the Commissioners would provide guidance to ERCOT regarding

the development of PGRR 145 at the Commission’s April 17, 2026, Open Meeting. Joint

Commenters support the Commission providing additional guidance, especially regarding

ERCOT’s proposal 1 not to include within the scope of previous studies for large load customers

that ERCOT deems fully complete and valid without additional review large loads that have been

included in Regional Planning Group (RPG) filings that are on the verge of approval by the Board

of Directors at their next meeting on April 20 and 21, 2026.

        Joint Commenters strongly agree with Oncor’s April 10, 2026, comments in this

proceeding recommending that all large loads that were studied as part of prior RPG filings and

have been approved by July 10, 2026, should be modeled as base loads not subject to additional

study under Section 9.2.1.1 of the proposed rule. 2 As Oncor clearly demonstrated in its comments,

these large loads already have been subjected to multiple study iterations and are far along in the

planning process. Rather than imposing a retroactive date of RPGs approved by March 4, 2026,


1
     See ERCOT April 4, 2026, Comments on PGRR 145, Section 9.2.1.4(3)(b), on page 53 of 90.
2
     Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s Comments on ERCOT’s PGRR 145 (April 10, 2026) at 2 (Oncor
     Comments).
 for this treatment, Joint Commenters respectfully support using a prospective date of RPG projects

approved by July 10, 2026. A prospective date to determine which RPG projects will be respected

in the Batch Zero process by considering their previous studies fully complete and valid without

additional review will appropriately take into account the significant effort, contractual and

financial commitments that have been made between load serving utilities and customers,

including for the procurement of long lead time equipment, and revisions to energization dates that

have been made as the large load and the utility have been studying and developing requirements

to interconnect.

        In its presentation filed on March 10, 2026, 3 in anticipation of the Commission’s Open

Meeting, ERCOT indicates that extending the date to allow large loads included in RPG filings

approved after March 4, 2026, to be modeled as base loads not subject to additional study under

Section 9.2.1.1 of the proposed rule could risk over-allocating capacity beyond what the ERCOT

system can reliably service. 4 Joint Commenters are confused by ERCOT’s assessment on this

point. The large loads that were studied in these RPG filings have supported the need for the

proposed transmission projects in the RPG filing and their energization dates already have been

adjusted to reflect the expected availability of the new transmission projects that will be approved.

In other words, the RPG filings are designed to serve the additional load that would be modeled

as base loads in the Batch Study Process, so by definition, the ERCOT grid will be able to reliably

serve the large loads studied in the RPG filing.

        Joint Commenters agree with Oncor’s assessment that ERCOT’s current proposal to cut

off the date of approved RPG filings to those approved by March 4, 2026, “creates uncertainty and




3
    ERCOT Batch Study Process for Large Load Interconnection, April 17, 2026 (filed April 10, 2026).
4
    Id. at page 6, Option C.

                                                                    Joint Commenter Comments – Page 2
 distrust among interconnecting customers and waste[s] ERCOT and customer resources to negate

years of studies and planning by forcing the full restudy of these loads.” 5

                                         CONCLUSION

       Joint Commenters appreciate the opportunity to provide these comments and respectfully

request the Commission to clarify that ERCOT should allow large load that were studied as part

of ERCOT RPG filings that have been approved by July 10, 2026, to be included in Batch Zero

and modeled as base loads not subject to restudy under Section 9.2.1.1 of the proposed rule.

                                              Respectfully submitted,

                                              ___________/s/__________________
                                              Brian Frazier
                                              Stream Data Centers, L.P.
                                              bfrazier@stream-dc.com
                                              (858) 204-1344

                                              ___________/s/__________________
                                              Justin Loth
                                              Provident Corp.
                                              jloth@provident.net
                                              (972) 385-4198


                                              Dated: April 16, 2026

    Oncor Comments at 2.
